types.title: Balance sheet value of purchased materials after a return

tasks.prompt:
The following economic events occurred at the company during the reporting period.
The company purchased spare parts worth 700 Th USD with a 14-day payment term.
Because of damage during the delivery, 15% of the spare parts were returned to the supplier.
Determine the balance sheet value of the spare parts after these events.
tasks.explanation: The purchase on credit increases the spare parts to 700 Th USD; the 15% return takes 105 Th USD back, so the balance sheet value is 700 - 105 = 595 Th USD. The payment term does not change the value.

tasks.prompt: Net income for the period appears on the:
options: Income Statement and Statement of Changes in Equity.
Balance Sheet and Statement of Cash Flows.
tasks.explanation: Net income is the result of the income statement and is added to retained earnings in the statement of changes in equity.

tasks.prompt: The ending balance in Contributed Capital appears on the:
options: Income Statement and Statement of Cash Flows.
Balance Sheet and Statement of Changes in Equity.
tasks.explanation: Contributed capital is an equity item: the balance sheet shows its ending balance and the statement of changes in equity shows its movement.

tasks.prompt: The ending balance in Accounts Receivable appears on the:
options: Statement of Changes in Equity only.
tasks.explanation: Receivables are assets; only the balance sheet shows their ending balance.

tasks.prompt: Sales revenue for the period appears on the:
options: Balance Sheet and Statement of Changes in Equity.
Statement of Changes in Equity only.
tasks.explanation: Revenue is an income statement item; only its result (profit) flows on to equity.

tasks.prompt: A general partnership is made up of:
tasks.explanation: The owners of a partnership are its partners.

tasks.prompt: A company limited by shares (Ltd.) is owned by:
tasks.explanation: The owners of a company limited by shares are the shareholders.

tasks.prompt: A sole proprietorship is owned by:
tasks.explanation: A sole proprietorship has exactly one owner.

tasks.prompt: Which form of business has an owner who is personally liable for all debts of the business?
tasks.explanation: A sole proprietor has unlimited personal liability; in the other forms the liability is limited.

tasks.prompt: Under the function of expense method, operating profit/loss is compiled using:
options: Net sales revenue - material type expenses - personnel type expenses - depreciation + other income - other expenses
Net sales revenue - direct cost of sales - indirect cost of sales + other income - other expenses
Net sales revenue - material type expenses - personnel type expenses - depreciation
tasks.explanation: The function of expense method groups costs by function: direct and indirect cost of sales.

tasks.prompt: Which of the following is NOT used when compiling operating profit under the nature of expense method?
tasks.explanation: Financial income belongs to the profit/loss from financial transactions, below the operating profit.

tasks.prompt: Profit/loss from financial transactions is compiled using:
tasks.explanation: It is the balance of financial income and financial expenses.

tasks.prompt: Profit or loss before tax is compiled using:
options: Operating profit + profit/loss from financial transactions
Profit/loss from financial transactions - tax expense
tasks.explanation: Operating profit plus the result of financial transactions gives the profit before tax.

tasks.prompt: For a trading company, revenue comes mainly from selling:
tasks.explanation: A trading company resells goods that it bought.

tasks.prompt: For a bank, revenue comes mainly from:
options: Interest and fees on financial services
tasks.explanation: A bank earns its income from financial services.

tasks.prompt: For a consulting firm, revenue comes mainly from:
tasks.explanation: A service provider sells services.

tasks.prompt: For a company that leases out machines, revenue comes mainly from:
tasks.explanation: The main activity is leasing, so the lease payments are the revenue.

types.title: Select the incorrect statement about an economic event

tasks.prompt: The company paid its trade payables from its bank account. Select the incorrect statement!
options: The company's balance sheet total increased.
The economic event does not affect the profit or loss account.
tasks.explanation: Assets and liabilities both decreased, so the balance sheet total decreased.

tasks.prompt: The owners paid additional capital into the company's bank account. Select the incorrect statement!
tasks.explanation: Contributed capital is equity, not a liability.

tasks.prompt: The company repaid part of its bank loan from its bank account. Select the incorrect statement!
options: The balance sheet total remained unchanged.
The company's equity did not change.
tasks.explanation: Assets and liabilities both decreased, so the balance sheet total decreased.

tasks.prompt: The company received a long-term bank loan into its bank account. Select the incorrect statement!
tasks.explanation: A loan is a liability; equity does not change.

tasks.prompt: From the following economic events, select which one qualifies as a complex economic event!
options: Interest on a bank loan was paid from the bank account.
A supplier invoice was settled by bank transfer.
Retained earnings were transferred to contributed capital.
The company withdrew cash from its bank account into the till.
tasks.explanation: A complex event affects both the balance sheet and the income statement; paid interest is an expense.

tasks.prompt: From the following economic events, select which one qualifies as a complex economic event!
options: Goods were sold on credit and the invoice was issued.
The owners increased the contributed capital by a bank transfer.
A customer paid an outstanding invoice by bank transfer.
A short-term loan was converted into a long-term loan.
tasks.explanation: The sale creates revenue (income statement) and a receivable (balance sheet).

tasks.prompt: From the following economic events, select which one qualifies as a complex economic event!
options: The company repaid a bank loan from its bank account.
The company purchased equipment on credit.
The company received an advance from a customer in cash.
The company paid salaries to its employees from the bank account.
tasks.explanation: Salaries are an expense: the event changes the balance sheet and the profit.

tasks.prompt: From the following economic events, select which one qualifies as a complex economic event!
options: Raw materials were purchased on credit.
Depreciation of machinery was recorded at year end.
Cash was deposited into the bank account.
The owners contributed capital in cash.
tasks.explanation: Depreciation is an expense and decreases the value of the machinery.
